medicina.titulo: Deep learning model using ECGs during sleep studies can predict cardiovascular outcomes
medicina.resumo: A research team supported by the National Institutes of Health (NIH) has found that electrocardiograms (ECGs) administered during sleep and paired with sleep stage information can be used to determine the risk of future adverse cardiac events. The study, which used a deep learning approach, suggests that using ECGs to predict which patients have a greater risk of poor heart-related outcomes could help guide clinical decision-making. The findings were published in the journal SLEEP.

medicina.titulo: STAT+: Pharmalittle: We’re reading about a setback for Argenx, Lilly suits over copycat versions of an obesity drug, and more
medicina.resumo: The FDA flagged a potential safety signal after four patient deaths in a trial testing a schizophrenia drug, Argenx faces an unusual setback, and more pharma news.

medicina.titulo: First real-world study of safety and quality of patient-facing AI in primary care
medicina.resumo: The aging population, workforce changes and patients' increasingly complex medical needs are all factors straining primary care systems around the world. Artificial intelligence tools have emerged as a potential means of extending the capabilities of health care workers, including in primary care settings. Large language models (LLMs), also known as chatbots, have performed extremely well in simulations. However, little is known about how these systems perform with real patients.

medicina.titulo: STAT+: Life Biosciences share glaucoma study updates for its cellular reprogramming drug
medicina.resumo: Life Biosciences said yesterday that three glaucoma patients have now received a single injection of its experimental cellular reprogramming drug, with no serious adverse events.

biologia.titulo: Tiny marine microbe sheds new light on how little genetic machinery a cell needs to survive
biologia.resumo: Scientists have discovered a previously unknown microorganism that has the smallest genome ever found and may be able to replicate and express its own genetic information.

biologia.titulo: How Does Life Unfold? A Landscape Metaphor Comes Into Its Own.
biologia.resumo: C.H. Waddington’s powerful image of embryonic stem cells specializing on a rolling landscape has captivated biologists since the 1950s. Experimental data is finally confirming, and complicating, his visionary ideas. The post How Does Life Unfold? A Landscape Metaphor Comes Into Its Own. first appeared on Quanta Magazine

biologia.titulo: New 'computational microscope' simulates DNA packaging at more than ten times previous scale
biologia.resumo: The DNA in our cells wraps around proteins called histones to form nucleosomes, which organize into chromatin. This organization helps pack genetic material into the nucleus and influences how easily genes can be read and DNA damage repaired. Understanding how chromatin changes requires studying molecular movements and interactions that are difficult to capture experimentally.

biologia.titulo: 3D genome 'entanglement' may explain how cephalopods evolved complex brains
biologia.resumo: Octopuses, squid and cuttlefish, collectively known as coleoid cephalopods, have evolved exceptionally large and elaborately structured nervous systems capable of complex behaviors such as problem-solving and rapid camouflage. A new study by scientists at the University of Vienna suggests that the origins of this complexity may lie not just in the genes themselves, but in how the genome is organized in 3D.

robotica.titulo: Two-armed robot throws and catches balls with human-like movements
robotica.resumo: Humans can move their limbs very rapidly and coordinate their movements with high precision to tackle specific manual tasks. While robots have become increasingly advanced in recent years, many of them remain less agile than humans and struggle to interact with moving objects of different shapes, weights and textures.

robotica.titulo: This Disembodied Hand Is All the Robot You Need
robotica.resumo: A hand attached to the end of an arm is a given for most humans, but what if robots didn’t have to play by the same rules as we do? Researchers from ETH Zurich have turned an off-the-shelf robotic hand into a completely self-contained robot that walks on its fingertips while using those same fingers to manipulate its environment. Besides making the perfect Halloween accessory for anyone planning to dress up as a member of the Addams Family—who were famously accompanied by a disembodied walking hand called Thing —this robotic hand could make it possible to operate controls and handle objects in places a traditional robot arm can’t reach, the researchers say. Soft Robotics Lab, ETH Zurich/YouTube Amirhossein Kazemipour , a Ph.D. candidate in the Soft Robotics Lab at ETH Zurich who led the project, believes this hand could prove useful in contexts like fiddly maintenance tasks in industrial settings, or in search and rescue, where a robot could detach its hand to explore confined spaces too tight for the rest of its body. computadores_pessoais.titulo: Is your graphics card getting too hot? This tip will boost its performance
computadores_pessoais.resumo: Graphics cards don’t simply die of old age — they usually suffocate due to neglect. The biggest enemy is dust, which settles on the cooling fins like an insulating layer and sabotages the cooling performance. However, before you take any action, you should carry out a professional diagnosis. Use the free tool Hwinfo for this. Launch the program in ‘Sensors only’ mode and look for the ‘GPU Hotspot Temperature’ reading under your graphics card. This reading represents the hottest spot directly on the silicon chip. Compare it with the normal ‘GPU Temperature,’ which is the average reading. A difference (delta) of more than 20 degrees Celsius under full load is a clear warning sign. It suggests that contact between the chip and the cooler is poor — for example, because the thermal paste has dried out or is unevenly distributed. If the delta is as high as 30 degrees Celsius or more, the card will already be significantly throttling its clock speed to prevent damage (thermal throttling). When carrying out PC maintenance, do pay special attention to your graphics card. After all, with the right GPU care, you can specifically prevent performance losses. inteligencia_artificial.resumo: O Google começa a limitar, nesta sexta-feira (9), os recursos disponíveis para usuários da versão gratuita do Gemini. A partir de agora, quem utiliza a inteligência artificial (IA) sem pagar uma assinatura perde o acesso aos modelos Flash e Pro , que passam a ser exclusivos dos planos pagos. A mudança também afeta assinantes do Google AI Plus, opção mais barata oferecida pela empresa. As restrições haviam sido anunciadas no início do mês, conforme noticiado pelo Canaltech . Segundo a página de suporte do Google, a atualização começa a valer hoje para contas pessoais sem assinatura, mas pode levar algum tempo para aparecer para todos os usuários. O que muda no Gemini gratuito? Com a atualização, quem não paga pelo Gemini fica limitado ao modelo Flash-Lite , versão mais leve da IA do Google, voltada para respostas rápidas e tarefas menos complexas. Até então, esses usuários também conseguiam utilizar o Flash e o Pro, embora com restrições de uso. O último é direcionado a atividades que exigem maior capacidade de raciocínio, como programação, análise de informações e resolução de problemas complexos. energia_materiais.resumo: Scientists have uncovered a hidden world of “in-between” materials that briefly form as chemical ingredients are heated, revealing structures that conventional methods can miss. Among the discoveries is a previously unknown form of bismuth vanadate, a material widely studied for using sunlight to help produce clean hydrogen. The new version has a different atomic structure and interacts with light in a strikingly different way, potentially opening new possibilities for solar fuels, catalysts, and electronics.
